newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court investigates scandal car crash.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court investigates scandal car crash.

text.p: A Turkish court is investigating possible links between the state and organised crime after an accident in which a police official and a wanted gangster were killed in the same car, a court official said on Thursday.

"We are now investigating the crash in Susurluk," the official told Reuters, confirming press reports that Istanbul state security court was looking into the relationship between those in the crash in the western town of Susurluk with a view to pressing charges of forming an organised crime group.

Turkey's interior minister, Mehmet Agar, resigned on Friday after the crash, in which a mobster wanted for political killings and drug dealing died in the same car as a senior security official and a former beauty queen.

Television showed pictures of reports sent by the Susurluk prosecutor to Istanbul, recommending an investigation into a crime ring due to the presence of guns, silencers and false identity documents in the car.
"We've done our duty. Now the affair is out of our hands," the prosecutor, Imdat Kacan, told the state-run Anatolian news agency. "Now we are just dealing with the accident itself."
His reports, also widely published in the media, said there were suspicious traces of white dust on a piece of newspaper and brown dust in a plastic bag recovered from the wreckage.
Turkish media speculated the dust particles could be traces of drugs.
The documents transferred to Istanbul include autopsy reports and witnesses' statements.

A Kurdish warlord, Sedat Bucak, who serves as a government MP, was injured in the crash. He is being treated in an Istanbul hospital, where members of the well-armed Kurdish tribe he heads are guarding him.

Associates say he is suffering from amnesia. Due to his parliamentary immunity he cannot be questioned against his will, even by the all-powerful state security courts, which deal with serious crimes including terrorism.
MPs voted on Tuesday for a parliamentary investigation into the affair and Agar's successor as interior minister, Meral Aksener, has promised his own inquiry.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his deputy Tansu Ciller have denied any link between the crash and the resignation. But Agar said he resigned to clear the way for a parliamentary investigation.
Media reports say Agar stayed in the same hotel as the crash victims in the Aegean resort of Kusadasi shortly before the accident.

Opposition MPs have said that Abdullah Catli, the gangster who died in the crash, carried a "green passport" -- given to state officials going abroad -- and demanded that police reveal who gave it to him.
The media quoted police records as showing that Catli, who had been on the run for nearly 20 years, had been arrested in August for firing in the air from a yacht but had been released the next day.
